newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico revises August trade surplus upwards.
newsitem.headline: Mexico revises August trade surplus upwards.

text.p: Mexico revised its August trade surplus upwards Friday to $353 million from a preliminary surplus reported of $264 million, the government said.
In August, exports totaled $7.879 billion against imports of $7.526 billion, the government said.
It said the data was revised upwards because of higher exports of electrical and electronic equipment.
Mexico's accumulated trade surplus for the year to August totalled $4.903 billion, the government added, after taking into account revised figures for June and July.
The surplus in June was revised upwards to $763 million from $749 million, and in July it went down from $438 million to $410 million.
The government also noted that August was the nineteenth month in a row that Mexico had chalked up a trade surplus.

In December 1994, an unexpected devaluation of the peso plunged Mexico into its worst economic recession in seven decades. Many economists said a burgeoning trade deficit during 1994 was one of the factors responsible for the devaluation.

Manufactured goods accounted for $6.723 billion of Mexico's August exports, or 85.3 percent of the month's total, itself up 10.8 percent on the year-ago amount. The Finance Ministry noted that auto exports for August were seasonally depressed by a changeover in annual models.
Crude oil exports accounted for $941 million in August, or 12.5 percent of the month's total, due to increases in both volume and export prices.
Agricultural exports were $175 million in August, down 12 percent from last year. Mining exports were $40 million.

August imports were up 17.5 percent on year-ago figures, an increase the Finance Ministry put down to "the recovery in aggregate demand and productive activity in the country, as well as the need for imported goods used in exports."
It also said farm exports had grown sharply. They were $3.084 billion in the first eight months, up 96 percent on the same period last year.

Intermediate goods accounted for $6.076 billion, or 80.7 percent of the month's total and were up 16.3 percent on last August. Capital and consumer goods accounted for $882 million and $568 million, respectively. Capital goods imports were up 22.3 percent over the same month a year ago, while consumer goods rose 22.9 percent.
